title: Buy The Dip In Brazil
text:
Buy The Dip In Brazil

Rohan Daswani

Gavekal Research | 26 Oct 2026

After Brazil’s first-round election, investors increasingly bet on a Flávio Bolsonaro victory and a tougher stance on public finances, driving Brazilian equities up more than 12% and Petrobras shares more than 11% (see The Bolsonaro Swing). But on Sunday, that fiscal-regime-change trade ran into a brick wall as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a surprise fourth term, narrowly defeating Bolsonaro in a runoff after overturning a first-round deficit of more than 2mn votes. Higher turnout among working-class voters appears to have been decisive.Flávio is seeking to have the election results annulled, reviving memories of his father Jair Bolsonaro’s attempts to overturn the 2022 election result. Markets look set to give back much of the first-round rally, with a Tokyo-listed Brazil equity exchange-traded fund down -15% in Monday trading, while the Brazilian real is expected to weaken by more than -10%. These are imperfect and illiquid proxies for where the Brazilian markets will open, but if they do paint an accurate picture of sentiment, circuit breakers should help to contain any panic selling. The central bank could also intervene directly in foreign exchange markets to stem a sharp decline in the real, although such measures would do little to resolve the underlying fiscal concerns adding to Brazil’s risk premium.
